summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and gastroparesis was admitted for severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and hyperglycemia with a glucose over 1300 mg/dL, diagnosed as hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state. She was treated in the MICU with IV fluids and an insulin drip, which was later transitioned to subcutaneous insulin. Her potassium was elevated at 7.6 and managed with medication. She experienced fluctuating glucose levels, requiring multiple insulin dose adjustments. Her blood pressure, initially in the 190s, improved with labetalol titration to 600 mg TID. A chest X-ray showed pulmonary edema, likely due to fluid overload and hyperglycemia, which resolved with treatment. She underwent successful placement of a left internal jugular port-a-cath due to chronic IV access difficulties. Her gastroparesis symptoms resolved with supportive care, and she tolerated oral intake. She was discharged home with updated insulin regimen, continued antihypertensives, and instructions to follow up with her endocrinologist.
problems: Diabetes with hyperosmolarity, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
